chunks: And by his chain, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'The stoning is in the Quran — the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "When the old man and the old woman commit adultery, then stone both of them without question, for indeed they have fulfilled the desire."'

key_terms.الرَّجْم: Rajm — stoning as a prescribed punishment in Islamic law for adultery committed by muhsan (previously-married) persons
key_terms.الشَّهْوَة: Al-shahwah — desire, lust; here indicating that by having been married, these individuals have had their physical desires legitimately fulfilled, making their transgression more grievous
key_terms.الشَّيْخ: Al-shaykh — in jurisprudential usage, a married or previously-married adult man; not simply 'old man'
key_terms.الشَّيْخَة: Al-shaykhah — a married or previously-married adult woman
key_terms.الْبَتَّة: Al-battah — an emphatic adverb meaning 'definitively', 'without exception', 'certainly'

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for stoning in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites a Quranic text on the punishment of stoning (rajm) for adultery committed by previously-married individuals. This narration addresses the classical jurisprudential debate about whether stoning has Quranic basis, with the Imam affirming it does and quoting a verse understood in Shia tradition as part of the original revelation. The terms 'shaykh' and 'shaykhah' here refer not merely to old age but to those who have experienced marriage and consummated it.

en.hubeali: And by his chain, form Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘The stoning is in the Quran, the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. When the old man and the old woman commit adultery, so stone both of them regardless, (because) for these two the lustful desire has expired’.
